items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Now, we had another boy named Wilson Miles

ctx.x: I didn't know that they were Turks but Farouk was a Turk, he wasn't Egyptian and we played for his wedding and I saw all those people and one of them looked like my aunt and she was just happy as she could be, the things that we were doing. In fact, we were the beloved, but Chitteson he almost got put in that thing again. They hesitated to let Chitteson go.

Now, we had another boy named Wilson Miles, well, they swear that he was from there, and Wilson Miles was there about two weeks and he was on the corner talking to the cabdrivers. He was just talking as if he were a citizen of the place, so all right, we all got our pay and got all our money

and got all our ladyfriend, and there were some English people who followed us all around and there was a certain girl, tall beautiful girl, but she was just tall and beautiful. Her name was Amy. Well, Amy could sing, she had a deep voice, you know, a contralto voice, but it was a pleasant voice, but she could sing beautifully. Now, on the ship coming back, everybody's happy. I think Burns had a case full of — , of cocaine which was nothing to — about, just nothing, just — and everybody was happy.
